description:
Terminal page -- an integrated multi-page, multi-tab PTY terminal with workflow generation, session transcript browsing, terminal output analysis, findings tracking, and concurrent session file conflict detection. Users can create multiple terminal pages (e.g., Development, Testing, Monitoring), each with its own independent zone layout, terminals, and saved configurations. Within each page, users execute shell commands in multiple concurrent terminal sessions organized in configurable zone layouts. The terminal supports session persistence across restarts (Claude Code session IDs are saved and auto-resumed), zone profiles that capture session assignments, shell integration for structured command history, keyboard shortcuts for efficient tab management, and an advisory file registry that auto-detects file conflicts across sessions, and plan implementation workflow execution from both the UI (Implement/Verify buttons) and CLI (run-plan-implementation.ts script).

# TerminalPage

## Asserting on terminal cell content (Claude Code, vim, htop, etc.)

DOM-search assertions in this spec (`assertionType: "exists"` with a
`textContent` criterion) **only see the runner's own UI chrome** — tab
bars, buttons, status indicators. They do **not** see what a TUI app
draws inside an xterm pane, because xterm.js renders to a canvas /
WebGL surface that's not in the DOM.

To assert on terminal cell content, query the server-side cell grid:

| Use case | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| Is text "Welcome" visible in any terminal? | `GET /ui-bridge/sdk/terminal/search?q=Welcome` |
| Is text "Welcome" in this specific session? | `GET /ui-bridge/sdk/terminal/search?q=Welcome&session_id=<id>` |
| Get the rendered text rows of a session | `GET /ui-bridge/sdk/terminal/sessions/<id>/buffer` |
| Get full cell-level grid (fg/bg/attrs/cursor) | `GET /ui-bridge/sdk/terminal/sessions/<id>/grid` |
| Compact text view for verifier prompts | `GET /ui-bridge/sdk/terminal/sessions/<id>/text` |
| Diff two sessions row-by-row | `GET /ui-bridge/sdk/terminal/sessions/<a>/diff/<b>` |

Full reference + worked examples:
[`src/components/terminal/GRID_TESTING.md`](../../../src/components/terminal/GRID_TESTING.md).
End-to-end smoke at `scripts/test-grid-endpoints.sh`.

The assertions in `spec.uibridge.json` below cover the runner UI
shell. Cell content lives on the HTTP side because the spec runner's
DOM-search primitive can't reach it.

## Spec maintenance

- Removed spec state `term-plan-cli-script` (2026-06-02): it asserted on plan-CLI *script output*, not page elements — a category error for a UI-Bridge page spec. The behavior it nominally covered is exercised by the Rust integration test `src-tauri/src/flywheel_e2e_tests.rs`.

## tmux work mode (plan `2026-10-11-runner-terminal-tmux-work-mode`)

States `tmux-one-session-on-screen` and `tmux-session-manager-navigator`,
transitions `enter-tmux-work-mode`, `tmux-swap-session` and
`exit-tmux-work-mode`.

- **Read the mode from the component, not the DOM.** `POST
  /ui-bridge/control/component/terminal-page/action/get-terminal-work-mode`
  returns `{mode, shownTabId, sidebarOpen}`; `set-terminal-work-mode` takes
  `{mode?: "grid" | "tmux"}` (omit to toggle). `get-zone-view-state` reads
  `layoutId: "single"` in tmux mode.
- **"Exactly one pane visible"** is observable per tab: only the shown tab's
  `terminal-input-<tabId>` and `terminal.close-session-<tabId>` have a
  non-zero rect, and there is no `terminal-zone-header-1`. The most recently
  shown off-screen panes stay mounted — up to `TMUX_WARM_TAB_LIMIT` (8, the
  WebGL context cap) besides the shown one; their `terminal-input-<tabId>` is
  registered with a 0×0 rect, so `registeredAt` is unchanged across a swap
  between them. A colder session has no `terminal-input-<tabId>` at all until
  it is shown, when it mounts and replays its scrollback ring.
- **Maximize is refused in tmux mode.** `maximize-zone` and
  `toggle-maximize-zone` fail with an error naming the mode rather than
  reporting `changed: true` for a view tmux already is.
- **A session manager row closes its session** through
  `terminal.session-card-close-<sessionId>` (a row with a live tab in this
  window only) — the way to close an off-screen session without showing it.
- **Output continuity** is checked by comparing the revealed pane's xterm
  buffer (`getScrollback` custom action on `terminal-input-<tabId>`) with the
  server grid (`GET /ui-bridge/sdk/terminal/sessions/<id>/text`), not by a
  DOM text search.
- **`GET /ui-bridge/control/snapshot` can time out in this state.** tmux
  mode opens the session manager, and with a large transcript corpus its
  Live view registers thousands of elements; measured 2026-10-11 on a temp
  runner, the snapshot exceeded its 10 s budget (5,596 registered elements)
  while `POST /ui-bridge/control/find` answered in ~2.4 s and
  `GET /ui-bridge/control/element/<id>` in < 100 ms. Use those two.

## Session organization (plan `2026-10-13-session-manager-chrome-style-tab-organization-and-operator-search`)

States `session-org-*` cover the Session Manager's group lens, group
headers (expanded / collapsed), Suggest groups, the query box and chips,
the Unknown tail, the search palette, the bulk bar, the Ready-to-close
banner, the close and force-close confirmations, Recently closed, the hover
card, the unseen dot and rail mode. Every transition carries its declared
`effect` in the IR (`state-machine.derived.json`); the bundled projection
drops `effect` by design (`projectIRToBundledPage`), so read the class from
the IR, from this table, or off the element's own `data-effect`.

- **Ids and effects have one source**: `SESSION_ORG_CONTROLS`
  (`src/components/terminal/sessionOrgControls.ts`) and
  `SESSION_QUERY_CONTROLS` (`sessionQueryChips.ts`). Every control renders
  `data-ui-bridge-id` and `data-effect`. Per-row / per-group controls append
  the id: `terminal.session-org.group-header-<groupId>`,
  `…group-collapse-<groupId>`, `…group-menu.close-group-<groupId>`,
  `…rail-item-<sessionId>`, `…unseen-dot-<sessionId>`,
  `…recently-closed.resume-<sessionKey>`, `…query-chip-<chipKey>`.
- **Destructive** (an autonomous walk must not fire them): `close`
  (row menu `session-menu.close`, component `session-org` `close`),
  `close-group` (`group-menu.close-group`, `session-org` `close-group`),
  `close-confirm`, `force-close-confirm`, `bulk.close`,
  `ready-to-close.review`. Close always goes through the confirmation and
  `graceful_exit`, never a kill (D7).
- **Write** (reversible org state, or starts a process): every group-menu
  item but Close group, every session-menu item but Close, the bulk bar's
  Finish / Add to group / New group / Pin / Unpin / Mute / Snooze / Move to
  page / Resume, `recently-closed.resume`, group collapse, `query-save-view`,
  `query-delete-view`, and the component actions `session-org`
  create/rename/recolor/move/ungroup/delete-group, set-group-collapsed,
  add-to/remove-from-group, set-pinned, set-muted, snooze, move-to-page;
  `session-group-suggestions` accept-suggestion / dismiss-suggestion /
  accept-all; `session-search-palette` activate.
- **Read**: chips, query input / clear, pickers, saved-view apply, the
  palette's search / close, Suggest groups (preview only), the rail toggle,
  the resize handle, the hover card, the unseen dot, bulk Clear, close
  Cancel, Force close (arms the second confirmation only), the Include and
  per-session ticks.
- **Drive org changes through `session-org`, not a drag.** Drag-and-drop
  is the operator's path; `POST
  /ui-bridge/control/component/session-org/action/<action>` (or the runner's
  `GET`/`POST /terminal/session-org`) is the deterministic one, and
  `list-groups` reads the store back.
- **Status words are two attributes, not one**: every row carries
  `data-session-location` and `data-session-activity`; `data-session-unseen`
  is `true` / `false` / `unknown` / `untracked`. A query row whose facts are
  unread is listed under the Unknown tail (`data-unknown-reason`), never
  counted as a non-match.
- **Hover card and unseen dot have no runnable jsdom test** on a box without
  `jsdom`; the Phase 8 temp-runner UI Bridge run is their live check.
- **What the UI Bridge can and cannot drive here** (measured on the Phase 8
  temp-runner run, 2026-10-14):
  - Context menus: `rightClick` on a row, and on a group header (which
    declares `GROUP_HEADER_ACTIONS`), opens the row / group menu. Builds
    before qontinui-runner `0c8290a10` refused every right-click on the control
    route. A menu closes when an item is chosen; a bridge `click` elsewhere
    does not dismiss it (it listens for `mousedown`).
  - Drag-and-drop is not advertised on rows or headers, so the `drag` action
    is refused — move sessions with `session-org` `add-to-group` /
    `move-group`.
  - Typing into `terminal.session-org.query-input` with `type` / `clear`
    edits the query (the box keeps its own draft, `sessionQueryDraft.ts`;
    before that, React restored the old text and the driver's second
    `onChange` wrote it back). `session-query` `set-query` remains the
    deterministic door.
  - The close dialog's buttons are re-registered per phase; after a close the
    result list's **Done** is `terminal.session-org.close-cancel`.
  - Recently closed lives in the **Previous** view, not the Live one.
  - Status of a fixture: an idle `claude` stand-in must draw the `❯` prompt on
    its cursor row, or `graceful_exit` refuses it ("not at an empty prompt")
    and nothing is closed — by design, never a kill.

groups.description: Users work with multiple concurrent terminal sessions organized as tabs. Each tab is an independent PTY session with its own shell, working directory, command history, and scrollback buffer. Users can create new tabs (Ctrl+Shift+T), close tabs (Ctrl+Shift+W), cycle between tabs (Ctrl+Tab), and rename tabs for better organization. Tabs auto-rename from the first command entered. On mount, the terminal attempts to reconnect to existing Rust PTY sessions from previous page visits, preserving shell state across navigation. When all tabs are closed, a helpful empty state guides users on how to create a new terminal. Conditional state: no terminals open (empty-state hint; rendered only when tabs.length === 0 at TerminalPage.tsx:768-777) — not rendered on the base terminal page, so it cannot match in a default snapshot (annotation pending the expectedConditionalStates baseline-waiver mechanism, plan §7).

groups.description: The terminal automatically analyzes output in real time to detect errors, warnings, test failures, and other notable findings. These are tracked per-session and displayed in a dedicated findings panel on the right side. Users can respond to findings (sending text back to the terminal), fix findings by spawning a new Claude Code session with the finding context pre-loaded, or batch-generate a workflow from multiple unresolved findings. groups.description: The Terminal page includes an advisory file conflict detection system that tracks which files are under active development by concurrent sessions (workflows and AI terminal sessions). When multiple sessions edit the same file, a warning banner appears below the notification bar showing conflicting files and which sessions hold them. Real-time toast alerts appear when a new conflict is detected (e.g., session B starts editing a file that session A already registered). The banner is collapsible â€” a summary line shows the count of conflicting files, and expanding reveals the full list with file paths and session names. The system auto-registers files when Claude Code uses Edit or Write tools, polls the runner's file registry API every 30 seconds, and listens for real-time Tauri events. The banner uses warning amber (#e0af68) coloring consistent with the 'needs-input' status style. Conditional state: a file conflict is currently active — not rendered on the base terminal page, so it cannot match in a default snapshot (annotation pending the expectedConditionalStates baseline-waiver mechanism, plan §7).

groups.description: Users can build and execute multi-stage plan implementation workflows directly from the Terminal page. assertions.description: Required element 0 for state Per-Tab Commit Traffic Light

target.label: Required element for Per-Tab Commit Traffic Light

groups.description: Each terminal tab that hosts an active Claude Code AI session displays a per-tab git "commit traffic light" + commit-progress button beside the existing file-lock icon (TerminalTabBar.tsx:~493). The traffic light is a small colored dot rendered by `<CommitTrafficLight>` (qontinui-runner/src/components/terminal/CommitTrafficLight.tsx) reflecting the session's git working-tree state restricted to the files THAT session has touched. Five states: `empty` (gray, default — tracker has no rows yet), `clean` (green — every touched file matches HEAD), `dirty` (yellow — at least one touched file differs from HEAD), `merging` (red — at least one touched repo has MERGE_HEAD/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD/REVERT_HEAD/rebase-merge/rebase-apply), and `unknown` (no dot rendered — backend probe failed or generated_at_ms is older than 5 minutes). Beside the dot, a GitCommit-icon button labeled "Commit progress" (button-commit-progress) is enabled only when status is `dirty`; on click, PTY tabs receive a multi-line `COMMIT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` typed via `writeToTerminal` that asks the AI to verify-and-commit only its own writes (cross-references its tool-call transcript, runs `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --stat` against the touched paths only, refuses to commit during in-progress merges, omits the Co-Authored-By trailer per the runner pre-commit hook). SDK chat sessions take the equivalent `send_user_message` Tauri invoke path. State source: the Tauri command `get_session_commit_state(taskRunId)` returns `{status, touched_count, dirty_count, repo_roots[], merging_repos[], generated_at_ms}` with lowercase status enum and snake_case fields. The `useCommitState` hook (qontinui-runner/src/components/terminal/useCommitState.ts) listens for `commit-state-changed` Tauri events `{type, task_run_id, state}` keyed by tab.claudeSessionId and additionally polls every 30 seconds. Events are emitted from three sites with a 500 ms per-session debounce: dispatcher.rs after every Edit/Write the SDK reports, mcp/ai_session.rs::commit_session_progress_inner success/no-op branches, and terminal/transcript_watcher.rs after the JSONL watcher records a new TouchedFile via pg.record_file_touched. The watcher backend (terminal/transcript_watcher.rs + extended terminal/transcript.rs parser) populates `coord.session_touched_files` for PTY-launched tabs, since `auto_register_file` in dispatcher.rs only fires for SDK-driven sessions; the watcher tails ~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/<session_id>.jsonl and parses Edit/Write/MultiEdit `tool_use` blocks. Workflow-spawned bypassPermissions sessions are filtered out via `is_workflow_session` so they never pollute the tracker. The `useTabSessionIdCapture` hook (qontinui-runner/src/components/terminal/useTabSessionIdCapture.ts) populates `tab.claudeSessionId` post-spawn by polling the existing `transcript_get_latest` Tauri command for ~15 s after `writeWhenReady` fires (PTY launches don't carry a session-id OSC — verified at `useShellIntegration.ts:67-118` and `TerminalInstance.tsx:699-704`; resumed sessions already have it set via `useShellIntegration.ts:135`). Without `claudeSessionId`, the traffic light wrapper still mounts but the state is treated as `unknown` and the button stays disabled. Conditional state: a tracked git change exists in the working tree — not rendered on the base terminal page, so it cannot match in a default snapshot (annotation pending the expectedConditionalStates baseline-waiver mechanism, plan §7).

metadata.conditionalOn: a tracked git change exists in the working tree

groups.name: Per-Tab Commit Traffic Light

groups.description: A PTY zone whose tab is bound to a Claude session shows the review panel (`SessionReviewPanel`, terminal/SessionReviewPanel.tsx), toggled from the zone title bar by the `terminal.review-toggle` button beside the prompts toggle; the tab's unread badge (`terminal.review-badge`) sits next to it and reads `n unread`, `?` when the change list or the read state could not be read, and is absent when there are no hunks. The panel overlays the zone with the same top/right orientation contract as the prompts panel (the two are mutually exclusive per tab). Its body is the shared file-changes list (`FileChangesPanel`) for `GET /sessions/{claudeSessionId}/file-changes`, headed by the base it was diffed against (e.g. `vs HEAD — committed work not shown`); each hunk (`terminal.review-hunk.<key12>`) carries an unread dot that is the explicit, reversible read toggle (`terminal.review-hunk-read.<key12>`) and an add-note button (`terminal.review-add-note.<key12>`). A hunk scrolled past inside an expanded file diff is marked read automatically unless the operator explicitly marked it unread. Its footer is the review send bar (`terminal.review-send-bar`): attached notes as chips (`terminal.review-chip.<noteId>`, detach `terminal.review-chip-detach.<noteId>`), a free-text line, Preview exact text, Send (`terminal.review-send`) and Insert without sending (`terminal.review-insert`).

groups.description: The Terminal page's tmux work mode (plan 2026-10-11-runner-terminal-tmux-work-mode, D1-D4): exactly ONE session is on screen, full size, in a single viewport (terminal/zone-grid/zoneCells.tsx — the same tab-keyed cells grid mode renders, so entering or leaving tmux mode remounts no terminal) and every other live session stays mounted off-screen at the `background` visibility tier, still running and still producing output. The layout is pinned to `single` (`get-zone-view-state` reads `{layoutId: "single", zoneCount: 1}`), so the page has exactly one zone header (`terminal-zone-header-0`) and no `terminal-zone-header-1`; only the shown tab's `terminal-input-<tabId>` and `terminal.close-session-<tabId>` have a non-zero rect. The viewport header carries the session name (full value in the title span's `title`) and its position `k / n` (`data-tmux-position="k/n"`, title `<name> — session k of n`). The CommandBar work-mode toggle (`terminal.work-mode-toggle`) reads `tmux` with `data-terminal-work-mode="tmux"` and `aria-pressed=true`. Read the mode without inferring it from the DOM through the `terminal-page` component action `get-terminal-work-mode` → `{mode: "tmux", shownTabId, sidebarOpen}`. The mode is entered/left by the toggle, Ctrl+Shift+Y, `/terminal.mode [grid|tmux]` (alias `/work-mode`) and the `set-terminal-work-mode` action (`{mode?: "grid"|"tmux"}`, omitted toggles; returns `{previousMode, mode, changed, sidebarOpened, message}`), and survives a page reload together with the session-manager sidebar. A newly created session is shown immediately; when the shown session closes, the most recently shown survivor replaces it (MRU, falling back to creation order). Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle the shown session. Picking a layout preset (Ctrl+Shift+1..8, the layout picker, `terminal.layout`) is an explicit grid request: it exits to grid mode, restoring the grid the operator left with the preset applied over it, so every live session is placed in a zone. The unzoned chip (`terminal.unzoned-chip-toggle`, "N more") is not rendered in tmux mode: off screen is the mode's normal state, and the session manager reaches every off-screen session.
groups.name: tmux Work Mode: One Session On Screen

assertions.description: The session manager's Live view is shown.

An off-screen live session row reads its location as hidden here (two-axis status), not a single-axis status.

groups.description: In tmux mode the session manager (opened on entering the mode) is the navigator, because it is the only way to reach an off-screen session (plan 2026-10-11-runner-terminal-tmux-work-mode, D5). Its Live view (`terminal.session-manager-view-live`) lists EVERY live session: Claude transcript rows and, for every live tab with no transcript row (a plain shell, or a Claude session not yet past 0 messages), a tab-sourced row (`data-session-source="tab"`, transcript-only actions hidden). Each row is a `terminal.session-card-<id>` button whose `data-session-on-screen` is `true` for exactly one row — the session on screen, which also carries the `on screen` badge (`data-testid="session-card-on-screen"`) and `aria-current="true"` — and `false` for the off-screen rows, which keep their status words so a hidden session needing you is visible from the list. Every row carries its two-axis status (plan 2026-10-13-session-manager-chrome-style-tab-organization-and-operator-search, D2) as `data-session-location` (`on-screen` | `hidden-here` | `outside-runner` | `other-device` | `not-running` | `unknown`) and `data-session-activity` (`needs-you` | `waiting-on-lock` | `working` | `idle-at-prompt` | `no-output-mid-tool` | `finished` | `exited` | `exited-error` | `unknown`), rendered as words (`data-testid="session-card-status"`): the on-screen row reads `on-screen`, a running off-screen row `hidden-here`, and a tab-sourced row's silence reads `idle-at-prompt` (an idle shell is not stuck). Clicking an off-screen row swaps it into the viewport; clicking the on-screen row is a no-op that still reports it selected.

states.description: Users work with multiple concurrent terminal sessions organized as tabs. Each tab is an independent PTY session with its own shell, working directory, command history, and scrollback buffer. Users can create new tabs (Ctrl+Shift+T), close tabs (Ctrl+Shift+W), cycle between tabs (Ctrl+Tab), and rename tabs for better organization. Tabs auto-rename from the first command entered. On mount, the terminal attempts to reconnect to existing Rust PTY sessions from previous page visits, preserving shell state across navigation. When all tabs are closed, a helpful empty state guides users on how to create a new terminal. Conditional state: no terminals open (empty-state hint; rendered only when tabs.length === 0 at TerminalPage.tsx:768-777) — not rendered on the base terminal page, so it cannot match in a default snapshot (annotation pending the expectedConditionalStates baseline-waiver mechanism, plan §7).

states.description: When a workflow is generated (from a session transcript, command history, or findings), a preview panel opens on the right side showing the full workflow structure. Users can review the generated workflow's phases and steps, then choose to execute it immediately, save it to the workflow library for later use, edit it in the Workflow Builder for refinement, or regenerate it with different parameters. The panel shows loading state during generation and error messages if generation fails. This workflow enables a rapid 'do it once in the terminal, then automate it' development pattern. Conditional state: a workflow has been generated via /generate against a live Claude session (not exercisable in spec-check, which invokes no AI) — not rendered on the base terminal page, so it cannot match in a default snapshot (annotation pending the expectedConditionalStates baseline-waiver mechanism, plan §7).

states.description: The terminal automatically analyzes output in real time to detect errors, warnings, test failures, and other notable findings. These are tracked per-session and displayed in a dedicated findings panel on the right side. Users can respond to findings (sending text back to the terminal), fix findings by spawning a new Claude Code session with the finding context pre-loaded, or batch-generate a workflow from multiple unresolved findings. The findings count badge on the action bar updates live as new issues are detected, keeping users aware of problems without interrupting their terminal workflow.
states.name: Real-Time Findings Detection

states.description: The terminal integrates AI analysis capabilities that process terminal scrollback, command history, and plan files to produce structured insights. Analysis types include: session summary (what happened in this terminal session), architecture review (system structure from plan files or terminal context), change impact (what files and systems were affected), progress tracking (how far along is the development plan), cross-tab analysis (correlating activity across multiple terminal sessions), and page architecture (analyzing the runner's own frontend). Analysis results appear in a dedicated panel with structured canvas-style panels. This transforms raw terminal output into actionable development intelligence.
states.name: AI-Powered Terminal Analysis

states.description: The Terminal page includes an advisory file conflict detection system that tracks which files are under active development by concurrent sessions (workflows and AI terminal sessions). When multiple sessions edit the same file, a warning banner appears below the notification bar showing conflicting files and which sessions hold them. Real-time toast alerts appear when a new conflict is detected (e.g., session B starts editing a file that session A already registered). The banner is collapsible â€” a summary line shows the count of conflicting files, and expanding reveals the full list with file paths and session names. The system auto-registers files when Claude Code uses Edit or Write tools, polls the runner's file registry API every 30 seconds, and listens for real-time Tauri events. The banner uses warning amber (#e0af68) coloring consistent with the 'needs-input' status style. Conditional state: a file conflict is currently active — not rendered on the base terminal page, so it cannot match in a default snapshot (annotation pending the expectedConditionalStates baseline-waiver mechanism, plan §7).

metadata.conditionalOn: a file conflict is currently active

states.name: File Conflict Detection Banner

states.description: Each session card in the SessionManagerPanel sidebar displays a file conflict warning icon when that session has files overlapping with other active sessions. The indicator shows a FileWarning icon in amber (#e0af68) with a numeric count badge showing how many conflicting files that session has. The count is derived from the file registry: for each file registered by this session, if any OTHER session also has that file registered, it counts as a conflict. The tooltip shows '{N} file(s) shared with other sessions'. Sessions with zero conflicts show no indicator. The conflict count is computed by the useFileConflicts hook's sessionConflictCounts Map, keyed by session task_run_id. states.description: Users can create multiple independent terminal pages, each with its own zone layout, terminals, labels, and saved configurations. A page tab bar at the top of the terminal area shows all pages. Clicking a page tab switches to that page by unmounting the current TerminalPage and remounting a new one connected to that page's PTY sessions. Each page's state (zone layout, labels, notes, pins, zone profiles, workspaces) is stored in page-namespaced localStorage keys. The default page uses un-prefixed keys for backward compatibility. PTY sessions are tagged with a page_id in the Rust backend, so each page only sees its own terminals.

states.description: Claude Code session IDs are persisted alongside terminal tab configurations. When the runner restarts and reconnects to existing PTY sessions, saved claudeSessionId values are merged back into the reconnected tabs and the sessions are auto-resumed with 'claude --resume <id>'. This ensures that Claude Code sessions survive runner restarts without manual intervention. The saved layout includes zone assignments, labels, notes, pins, and Claude session IDs per tab.
states.name: Session Persistence & Auto-Resume

states.description: Each terminal page has isolated storage for its configuration. Zone layouts, session persistence, zone profiles, workspaces, zone labels/notes/pins, and grid column/row ratios are all namespaced by pageId. The default page uses un-prefixed keys (backward compatible), while non-default pages use 'page:{pageId}:' prefixed keys. This ensures that creating a zone profile on page A does not appear when viewing page B's profiles.
states.name: Per-Page Storage Isolation

states.description: Users can build and execute multi-stage plan implementation workflows directly from the Terminal page. Two entry points exist: (1) from a transcript panel, select messages containing a plan and click Implement to build a workflow with implement/review/next-steps stages per phase, or (2) from the status bar, click Implement next to a detected plan file. The Implement button (amber, Rocket icon) is the primary action; the Verify button (gray, ListChecks icon) builds a lighter verification-only workflow. Both parse the plan markdown into phases and tasks, build a multi-stage UnifiedWorkflow, and show it in the workflow preview panel for execution. Conditional state: a plan file is loaded AND the plan-build panel is open; the Implement/Verify buttons migrated to the /plan-implement and /plan-verify slash commands when the ZoneStatusBar toolbar was removed — not rendered on the base terminal page, so it cannot match in a default snapshot (annotation pending the expectedConditionalStates baseline-waiver mechanism, plan §7).

states.description: Each terminal tab that hosts an active Claude Code AI session displays a per-tab git "commit traffic light" + commit-progress button beside the existing file-lock icon (TerminalTabBar.tsx:~493). The traffic light is a small colored dot rendered by `<CommitTrafficLight>` (qontinui-runner/src/components/terminal/CommitTrafficLight.tsx) reflecting the session's git working-tree state restricted to the files THAT session has touched. Five states: `empty` (gray, default — tracker has no rows yet), `clean` (green — every touched file matches HEAD), `dirty` (yellow — at least one touched file differs from HEAD), `merging` (red — at least one touched repo has MERGE_HEAD/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD/REVERT_HEAD/rebase-merge/rebase-apply), and `unknown` (no dot rendered — backend probe failed or generated_at_ms is older than 5 minutes). Beside the dot, a GitCommit-icon button labeled "Commit progress" (button-commit-progress) is enabled only when status is `dirty`; on click, PTY tabs receive a multi-line `COMMIT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` typed via `writeToTerminal` that asks the AI to verify-and-commit only its own writes (cross-references its tool-call transcript, runs `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --stat` against the touched paths only, refuses to commit during in-progress merges, omits the Co-Authored-By trailer per the runner pre-commit hook). SDK chat sessions take the equivalent `send_user_message` Tauri invoke path. State source: the Tauri command `get_session_commit_state(taskRunId)` returns `{status, touched_count, dirty_count, repo_roots[], merging_repos[], generated_at_ms}` with lowercase status enum and snake_case fields. The `useCommitState` hook (qontinui-runner/src/components/terminal/useCommitState.ts) listens for `commit-state-changed` Tauri events `{type, task_run_id, state}` keyed by tab.claudeSessionId and additionally polls every 30 seconds. Events are emitted from three sites with a 500 ms per-session debounce: dispatcher.rs after every Edit/Write the SDK reports, mcp/ai_session.rs::commit_session_progress_inner success/no-op branches, and terminal/transcript_watcher.rs after the JSONL watcher records a new TouchedFile via pg.record_file_touched. The watcher backend (terminal/transcript_watcher.rs + extended terminal/transcript.rs parser) populates `coord.session_touched_files` for PTY-launched tabs, since `auto_register_file` in dispatcher.rs only fires for SDK-driven sessions; the watcher tails ~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/<session_id>.jsonl and parses Edit/Write/MultiEdit `tool_use` blocks. Workflow-spawned bypassPermissions sessions are filtered out via `is_workflow_session` so they never pollute the tracker. The `useTabSessionIdCapture` hook (qontinui-runner/src/components/terminal/useTabSessionIdCapture.ts) populates `tab.claudeSessionId` post-spawn by polling the existing `transcript_get_latest` Tauri command for ~15 s after `writeWhenReady` fires (PTY launches don't carry a session-id OSC — verified at `useShellIntegration.ts:67-118` and `TerminalInstance.tsx:699-704`; resumed sessions already have it set via `useShellIntegration.ts:135`). Without `claudeSessionId`, the traffic light wrapper still mounts but the state is treated as `unknown` and the button stays disabled. Conditional state: a tracked git change exists in the working tree — not rendered on the base terminal page, so it cannot match in a default snapshot (annotation pending the expectedConditionalStates baseline-waiver mechanism, plan §7).

metadata.conditionalOn: a tracked git change exists in the working tree

states.description: A PTY zone whose tab is bound to a Claude session shows the review panel (`SessionReviewPanel`, terminal/SessionReviewPanel.tsx), toggled from the zone title bar by the `terminal.review-toggle` button beside the prompts toggle; the tab's unread badge (`terminal.review-badge`) sits next to it and reads `n unread`, `?` when the change list or the read state could not be read, and is absent when there are no hunks. states.description: In tmux mode the session manager (opened on entering the mode) is the navigator, because it is the only way to reach an off-screen session (plan 2026-10-11-runner-terminal-tmux-work-mode, D5). Its Live view (`terminal.session-manager-view-live`) lists EVERY live session: Claude transcript rows and, for every live tab with no transcript row (a plain shell, or a Claude session not yet past 0 messages), a tab-sourced row (`data-session-source="tab"`, transcript-only actions hidden). Each row is a `terminal.session-card-<id>` button whose `data-session-on-screen` is `true` for exactly one row — the session on screen, which also carries the `on screen` badge (`data-testid="session-card-on-screen"`) and `aria-current="true"` — and `false` for the off-screen rows, which keep their status words so a hidden session needing you is visible from the list. Every row carries its two-axis status (plan 2026-10-13-session-manager-chrome-style-tab-organization-and-operator-search, D2) as `data-session-location` (`on-screen` | `hidden-here` | `outside-runner` | `other-device` | `not-running` | `unknown`) and `data-session-activity` (`needs-you` | `waiting-on-lock` | `working` | `idle-at-prompt` | `no-output-mid-tool` | `finished` | `exited` | `exited-error` | `unknown`), rendered as words (`data-testid="session-card-status"`): the on-screen row reads `on-screen`, a running off-screen row `hidden-here`, and a tab-sourced row's silence reads `idle-at-prompt` (an idle shell is not stuck). Clicking an off-screen row swaps it into the viewport; clicking the on-screen row is a no-op that still reports it selected.
states.name: tmux Session Manager Lists Every Live Session

transitions.name: Swap the on-screen session from the session manager

states.description: The Session Manager's default lens (`terminal.session-manager-group-by` = `groups`, plan 2026-10-13-session-manager-chrome-style-tab-organization-and-operator-search, Phase 3): user groups first, then the Ungrouped section, with Suggest groups in the header. Conditional state: the Session Manager is open on its Live view with the group lens.
states.name: Session Manager Group Lens

target.accessibleName: Collapse the Session Manager to a rail

states.description: Suggest groups opens a preview of deterministic suggestions for ungrouped sessions (by plan, PR, repo+branch or repo; no AI). Nothing is created until a suggestion is accepted. Component `session-group-suggestions`: list-suggestions (read), accept-suggestion / dismiss-suggestion / accept-all (write). Conditional state: Suggest groups was clicked.
states.name: Suggested Session Groups Dialog

states.description: A user group renders a header (`terminal.session-org.group-header-<groupId>`) carrying `data-group-id`, `data-group-title`, `data-group-color-role` (one of the six group color roles, never a status color), `data-group-collapsed`, `data-group-member-count` and `data-group-needs-you-count`; its right-click menu holds Rename, Color, Collapse, New session in group, Move to page, Ungroup, Close group (destructive) and Delete group. Conditional state: a user group exists.
states.name: User Group Header (Expanded)

states.description: A collapsed group renders only its header; its members are not rendered (and so cannot be swept into a Shift range or Ctrl+A), while the header still shows how many members need input (`data-group-needs-you-count`). Conditional state: a user group is collapsed.
states.name: User Group Header (Collapsed)

states.description: The query box (D5 grammar: is:, where:, repo:, plan:, group:, title:, text:"…", idle>30m, OR, -negation) with one-click chips that toggle a token (Needs you, Working, Idle, No output, Finished, Ready to close, Outside runner, Pinned) and show matched / unknown counts (`data-count`, `data-unknown-count`, `aria-pressed`). The bar's `data-query` and `data-query-ok` mirror the parse. Component `session-query`: get-query / set-query / clear-query / toggle-chip (read), save-view / delete-view (write). Conditional state: the Session Manager is open on its Live view.
states.name: Session Query Box and Chips

transitions.name: Save the query as a view

states.description: When a query cannot be decided for some rows (a fact source unread), those rows are listed separately under the Unknown tail with the reason (`data-unknown-reason`) — never silently counted as non-matching. Conditional state: the active query has rows it cannot decide.
states.name: Query Unknown Tail

states.description: Ctrl+Shift+Space (or `/sessions.find`) opens a palette searching live, previous and recently-closed sessions by title, topic, repo or transcript text. Component `session-search-palette`: search (read), activate (write: focuses a live session or resumes another), close (read). Conditional state: the palette was opened.
states.name: Session Search Palette

states.description: Selecting rows (click, Ctrl/Shift-click, Space, Ctrl+A, or Select all N shown) shows the bulk bar (`data-selected-count`): Close (destructive — opens the named confirmation), Finish, Add to group, New group, Pin, Unpin, Mute, Snooze, Move to page, Resume (write) and Clear (read). Conditional state: at least one row is selected.
states.name: Session Bulk Action Bar

states.description: When sessions are finished (closable), a banner (`data-ready-count`) offers Review, which opens the close confirmation listing each with why it is finished. Conditional state: at least one live session is finished.
states.name: Ready to Close Banner

states.description: Every close path (row, group, bulk, Ready to close) goes through one confirmation that names each session, with a per-session Include tick; Close re-checks each item before acting and ends sessions through graceful_exit, never a kill. A session that is working requires Force close plus its second tick (D7). Conditional state: a close was requested.
states.name: Close Confirmation

states.description: Force close arms a second confirmation for sessions that are still working; it is destructive and still graceful_exit-only. Conditional state: Force close was clicked in the close confirmation.
states.name: Force Close Confirmation

states.description: Closed sessions are listed under Recently closed (`data-shown-count`, `data-total-count`) with Resume (`terminal.session-org.recently-closed.resume-<sessionKey>`, write), whose outcome is read back (`data-reopen-state`). Conditional state: a session was closed from this runner.
states.name: Recently Closed Sessions

states.description: Hovering a row (or a rail item) opens a card with the session's repo, branch, PRs and why it is in its current state; each field is `data-hover-field=<key>` with `data-unknown` when its source is unread. Conditional state: a session row is hovered.
states.name: Session Hover Card

states.description: A session that produced output while not focused carries `data-session-unseen="true"` and an unseen dot (`terminal.session-org.unseen-dot-<sessionId>`) until it is focused; an unread source reads `unknown`, never `false`. Conditional state: a session produced output while unfocused.
states.name: Unseen Activity Dot

states.description: Collapsed to a rail, the panel shows one status dot per rendered row (`terminal.session-org.rail-item-<sessionId>`, with location/activity/unseen attributes); hovering an item opens the hover card. Conditional state: the panel was collapsed to a rail.
states.name: Session Manager Rail Mode
